original_test_intent: Verify the Type 4 Thread Count for each populated processor, including the extended Thread Count 2 encoding when applicable, matches the approved enabled-core and SMT topology and remains correct after reboot.
original_method: Capture complete raw/decoded Type 4 records, derive the effective thread count from legacy and extended fields, bind it per socket, compare with approved enabled cores and threads-per-core/SMT policy plus scoped OS topology, reboot and repeat without changing SMT or CPU state.
manual_activity: A user approves per-socket thread counts, SMT/core relationship, extended-field/unknown rules, OS correlation and reboot plan. Core verification is automatable.
required_inputs: Expected effective thread count per populated processor/socket
Applicable SMBIOS version and legacy Thread Count versus Thread Count 2 rule
Approved SMT enabled/disabled policy and threads-per-enabled-core relationship
Treatment of unknown zero values and OS offline/visibility differences
Validated SMBIOS/OS topology tools plus approved reboot and OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: Use read-only SMBIOS and OS topology queries; do not toggle SMT, online/offline CPUs or modify BIOS/firmware.
Preserve raw legacy/extended thread fields and formatted length so sentinel or truncation defects remain visible.
Keep logical threads distinct from total and enabled physical cores; apply consistency math only under the approved SMT policy.
Do not treat an OS online CPU mask as the SMBIOS Thread Count without accounting for offline/isolated/virtualized visibility.
Stop on invalid selector combinations, impossible core/thread relationships, mapping ambiguity, drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Resolve effective Type 4 Thread Count per socket, validate approved SMT/core relationships and optionally correlate layer-aware OS topology before/after reboot.
Do not change SMT/CPU state, force a topology to match or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the expected thread/SMT topology, unknown handling and permitted OS visibility differences.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The label is correct, but grep loses raw legacy/extended fields and socket context and cannot validate threads against enabled cores and SMT policy.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture full raw/decoded Type 4 records, compute effective Thread Count with version/length checks and compare it per socket with approved enabled-core and threads-per-core topology.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Thread Count scope, Type 4 script and 10/10-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.status: EXTENDED THREAD COUNT AND SMT CONSISTENCY VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Decode Thread Count/Thread Count 2 using raw values and formatted length, bind each result to a populated socket and validate the approved SMT relationship to enabled cores; retain OS topology only as scoped corroboration.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 4 systems, including thread counts exceeding the legacy one-byte range.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS/SMT policy, CPU SKU/topology, parser/dmidecode and OS versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 4 Thread Count and Thread Count 2 semantics, approved CPU/SMT topology and installed tool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds extended encoding, explicit unknown handling and core-to-thread consistency rather than checking a displayed number alone.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; detects truncated counts and inconsistent SMT topology.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS-visible logical CPUs can differ due to boot limits, hotplug, virtualization or isolation; differences require layer-aware evidence.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve SMT-off, SMT-on or SKU-specific thread ratios per socket, but must not substitute total cores, enabled cores or a transient OS online count for the Type 4 thread field.
expected_evidence: Approved per-socket thread/SMT/core matrix, extended-field rule, unknown policy and tool versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 4 table with raw legacy/extended fields, formatted length and effective Thread Count
Consistency calculation against enabled cores and approved threads-per-core, with scoped OS topology evidence
Approved reboot/health evidence and equivalent post-reboot comparison
Engineer verdict with any documented OS visibility exception

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item and criterion consistently target Thread Count; missing SMT/topology values are readiness inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The fields and relationships are machine-checkable once approved topology policy is supplied.

review_improvement: Prevents a decoded count from concealing truncation and prevents OS online CPUs from being mistaken for the firmware-owned total thread field.
independent_technical_reasoning: With an approved SMT/topology matrix, collection, effective-value calculation, consistency checks and persistence comparison are software-controlled.
